chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who has a debt upon him and in his hand is wealth belonging to others. Is Zakat upon him? He said: If it is a loan, and a year passes over it, then he should purify it (pay Zakat).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Zakat on debt or loans held in one's possession?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific condition for Zakat liability on debt: the debt must be a loan (*qard*) that has been outstanding for a full lunar year (*hawl*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between general debts and specific loans, emphasizing that Zakat is due on the debtor's wealth once the time period for the loan has elapsed, reflecting the principle that financial obligations are settled through the passage of time rather than immediate deduction.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about a man upon whom are debts and in his hand is wealth of theirs’. Is the Zakāt upon him?’
So heasws said: ‘When it was a loan, and a year passes by over it, so he should purify it (pay Zakāt)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Sama‘ah and from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Alfah who has said the foiiowing: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who owes a loan and in his hands is the assets of another person. Is he required to pay Zakat for the asset of other people? He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is loan and it has remained in his hand for one year, he then is required to pay its Zakat.’”
